summary: The exact verified launch revision correctly limits anonymous callers to a fixed illustrative scenario and database-local effects; protects reset, communication initiation, and manual tick routes with separate server-side credentials; validates provider signatures over raw bounded bodies; deduplicates and orders callbacks; parameterizes SQL; minimizes caregiver data; fails ML closed; excludes secrets from the browser bundle and tracked files; and has zero reported production dependency vulnerabilities. Approval is withheld because the scheduled-action path can create provider outbox work without an operator-authenticated communication authorization, public PostgreSQL URLs accept sslmode=disable, and the consequential manual-tick credential has no enforced minimum strength.

findings.description: runTick materializes every due scheduled_action directly into the provider outbox at lines 258-274 without verifying or persisting authorization_source=operator_control. The deterministic reset seeds two such SMS schedules in database/migrations/20260920172033_launch_workflow_core.sql even though reset records external_actions_suppressed=true. This bypasses the architecture rule that provider dispatch authorization originates only in an operator-authenticated communication command.
findings.impact: After the global and SMS switches are enabled, a due or overdue reset-seeded action can send to the allowlisted real recipient solely because the scheduler is running; there is no auditable per-action operator communication authorization and reset can indirectly lead to a later external effect.
findings.remediation: Keep reset-created cadence records inert. Require every outbox row capable of provider dispatch to reference an authorization record produced by POST /api/v1/communications/{sms|voice}, persist and constrain authorization_source=operator_control at the database boundary, and make scheduled materialization reject or retain unauthorized work without crossing the provider boundary. Add integration/database tests proving reset and due schedules cannot produce dispatchable outbox work until an operator-authenticated communication command authorizes the exact stable action.

findings.description: assertDatabaseUrl treats the mere presence of an sslmode query parameter as sufficient for a non-local, non-Railway-private PostgreSQL host. A public URL with sslmode=disable is accepted even though the error contract says public connections must require TLS.
findings.impact: A deployment misconfiguration can send database credentials and controlled workflow data over a non-TLS public connection while health/config validation reports success.
findings.remediation: Reject sslmode values that do not require certificate-protected transport (including disable, allow, and prefer), or construct the pg client with an explicit reviewed TLS policy for every non-local, non-.railway.internal host. Add positive private-Railway/local cases and a negative sslmode=disable test.

findings.description: The manual scheduler endpoint rejects an empty CRON_SECRET but accepts any non-empty value; unlike ONCOREADY_OPERATOR_TOKEN, no minimum strength is enforced even though project setup requires at least 32 random bytes.
findings.impact: A weak or accidentally truncated deployment value can be guessed to invoke a consequential scheduler cycle, which may process provider work once external actions are enabled.
findings.remediation: Fail closed unless CRON_SECRET meets the same reviewed minimum entropy/length policy as the operator token, validate it during privileged-route/runtime preflight, and add tests showing short values return dependency_unavailable rather than authenticating.
